December 5th, 1966. 
ILE PERROT DAY CAMP TO HOUSE EXPO VISITORS 
a tetanic ed Edad 


On November 8th, work was officially started on facilities which will 
enable the 'Y' day camp at Ile Perrot to accommodate a total of 120,000 visitors 
during Expo '67, 


Charles Morrison, Chairman of the Montreal YMCA Expo-Centennial Committee, 
turned the first sod. He did so unhurriedly, on schedule, despite intermittent 
rain which increased to a heavy downpour just minutes before he started, 


The development involves 90 trailer sites, 100 camp sites, an outdoor 
swimming pool and sanitary facilities, changing and electrical power sources, 


After the World's Fair ends, the new facilities will enable the 
Montreal 'Y' to expand its summer program at Ile Perrot, Ultimate objective 
is to establish a year-round leadership training centre at that site, 


Among the many others who disregarded the weather to participate in the 
ceremony were two members of Quebec's Legislative Assembly; Paul Gerin-Lajoie, 
former Minister of Education, and A. Séguin, who is still Mayor of Pointe Claire, 


RENOVATION OF DOWNTOWN 'Y' RESIDENCE CONTINUES 
—_—— eee ee 


The Building Committee has approved plans to renovate entirely the ninth 
floor of the Stanley Street Residence, This floor, with its 44 rooms, will be 
the fifth of the 10 floors in the building to be completely modernized, To- 
gether, the rooms in this building and those on the sixth floor of the Drummond 
Street Residence can accommodate a total of 504 persons, 


OUT OF BRANCH LANGUAGE PROGRAM POPULAR 
Be ic nd Laid ncn thee enad  tBaadrin 8 
Ward Minielly, Adult Education Director at the International Branch, 


estimates its out-of-branch language program has to date helped some 320 
persons learn or perfect their command of either English or French, 


pa 


Under this program, which was launched in 1964, classes are conducted 
for participating companies on their own premises. 


First to take advantage of these courses was Dominion Rubber (now 
Uniroyal), which was followed in quick succession by Sherbrooke Paper Products, 
Dominion Textiles, Steinberg's and CPR. 


Newest participant is La Societé des Artisans Coopérative d‘*Assurance 
de Vie, which has enrolled 32 employees in an English course and will sign up 
another 30 for a similar course to be started in February. 


CATHOLIC LEADER PRAISES YMCA 


Father Irénée Beaubien has declared himself one of the growing number 
of religious and community leaders who feel the YMCA can contribute significant- 
ly to the lowering of barriers between people of various beliefs and cultures, 


“Here the YMCA has a definite role to play", said Father Beaubien, who 
is Director of the Montreal Ecumenical Centre and a member of the Board of the 
National Secretariat on Ecumenism, 


Father Beaubien also said he considers the YMCA as one of the leading 
world Associations dedicated to serving the spiritual, intellectual and 
physical needs of people, especially youth. 


"The time has come for the 'Y' and similarly-motivated Roman Catholic 
Associations to enter into dialogue, and see what can be done, cooperatively, 
to better serve the needs of the community", he suggested. 


FREEDOM AND RESPONSIBILITY 


Freedom and its accompanying responsibilities will be the theme of a 
conference being planned by teen-age members, adult leaders and Board and 
Committee members of Lachine-Dorval Branch, 


The stage was set for such a conference by the creation of a "Y-Not™ 
coffee house in the Branch'ts teen lounge. Purpose of this coffee house is 
to give young people an opportunity to develop and administer the type of 
program they desire in an atmosphere conducive to the sharing of ideas, 
concerns and aspirations, 


Plans are to hold the conference out of town, over a weekend, 


-3- 


COMMUNITY STUDY APPROVED 


Lakeshore Branch and the Applied Social Science Department of Sir 
George Williams University will head a study involving all community organ- 
izations in the City of Beaconsfield, which approved a $2,500, grant for this 
purpose, 


Objectives of the study are: 


To determine how the various community groups can cooperate 
more fully to solve the unmet needs that are identified. 


To identify what types of facilities are needed now, and 
will be required in the future. 


To find ways to promote better understanding and lines 
of communication between adults and young people,
